DDE drift scores

Source: R/dfr_dde.R
dde_score.Rd

Predicts the drift score of unmonitored features from the drifting monitored features (Szucs and Nemeth, 2025, Eq. 25).

Usage

dde_score(curve, data, drifting, unmonitored)

Arguments

curve

DDE curve, as returned by dde_curve().

data

Data frame or matrix with the features in the reference window, where the Pearson correlations are measured.

drifting

Names of the monitored features that drift.

unmonitored

Names of the features to score.

Value

named numeric vector of scores, one per unmonitored feature.

Details

The score of an unmonitored feature \(f_i\) is the mean, over the drifting monitored features \(f_j\), of the DDE probability at \(|\rho_{ij}|\): the probability of the largest threshold that does not exceed the correlation. Thresholds without pairs take the probability of the previous threshold. Scores are limited to \([0, 1]\); they are 0 when no monitored feature drifts.

Examples

set.seed(1)
a <- stats::rnorm(200)
b <- stats::rnorm(200)
data <- data.frame(a1 = a, a2 = a + stats::rnorm(200, sd = 0.2),
                   a3 = a + stats::rnorm(200, sd = 0.5),
                   b1 = b, b2 = b + stats::rnorm(200, sd = 0.2),
                   b3 = b + stats::rnorm(200, sd = 0.5))
curve <- dde_curve(data, c("a1", "a2", "a3"))
# a1 drifts: its neighbours get high scores, the "b" features low ones.
dde_score(curve, data, drifting = "a1", unmonitored = c("a2", "a3", "b2", "b3"))
#>  a2  a3  b2  b3 
#> 1.0 1.0 0.4 0.4
